parsed.explanation: The combined regime's worst traveller-facing features are state-imposed and universal, not scattered: entry documents that cannot be made to match presentation (no X marker; markers not matching birth sex refused; discrepancy treated as reasonable doubt and possible material misrepresentation carrying lifetime inadmissibility), facility access by birth sex criminal in four states with a documented arrest and men's-ward detention, and documented severe harm in immigration custody. Courts have enjoined parts of the programme and a national hate-crime statute covers gender identity, so recourse is real but partial and contested. Severe social hostility is not the driving signal; the state's own instrumentalities are. That places it below the administrative-denial-only anchors and above the severe-tier anchors, while falling short of the reduced-risk band because at least one documented harmful practice is unremedied.

entry_documents.exposure: No X markers issued; markers not matching birth sex refused; discrepancy triggers refusal and requests for more evidence, and suspected wilful misrepresentation can support a permanent lifetime inadmissibility finding. Travellers report passports blocked or confiscated; trans athletes barred.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; misrepresentation findings are never automatic and require four elements; litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-country passport meets national adjudication; a document mismatch can escalate to a fraud finding and then to detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse reported. National corrections policies adopted from 2026 include hair removal and hormone withdrawal.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Corrections order is under challenge; some executive orders enjoined; waiver possibilities exist for fraud findings.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border discrepancy can route a visitor into immigration custody, where the documented harms sit.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans by birth sex in 9 states across all government buildings, 9 more covering schools and some buildings, 3 schools-only; criminal in 4 states. One documented arrest, handcuffed, held 24 hours in a men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 units and the capital district have no mapped ban; one statute requires wilful entry plus refusal to depart and lists exemptions.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Operative rule differs by state visited; the harshest applicable rule governs the itinerary.

care_services.exposure: Division: under-18 transition care banned by statute with licence revocation; a coastal-city hospital cancelled all gender-affirming surgeries in February 2025, including a 24-year-old's pre-approved mastectomy. National funding freeze.
care_services.protection: Public-employee plan settlement requires coverage of medically necessary care, including for minors treated outside the state.
care_services.interaction: Resident-facing care rules; visitor access to emergency or routine care is not documented in either direction.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'rapid neutralization' of 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; December 2025 reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology'; curricula and materials purged.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; the ideology phrase is not a reward criterion; no documented prosecution of a trans visitor.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Frames institutional posture rather than a direct checkpoint mechanism, but colours how officials may read a flagged visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: A minor's documents face the same marker screening; division bans clinician-delivered care for under-18s; executive order targets facilitators of a minor's social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented instance of a visiting family detained or prosecuted; plan coverage can extend to out-of-state care.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces combined document screening plus possible scrutiny of the child's records.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Three violent crimes against trans women in one city in 2023, two fatal within a week; department called it epidemic-level; state-level bias statutes cover gender identity in only 23 states.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; police opened and pursued investigations; the 4.8/100k figure is an explicit undercount floor and carries no magnitude.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police response is the operative remedy; national statute supplies a fallback.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforceability shifts with litigation; which measures operate at the moment of travel is unresolved; hospital surgery suspension's permanence unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several orders; passport policy challenged by seven plaintiffs; civil-liberties FAQ published.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Relief is real but ex post and uneven; a traveller cannot rely on a pending injunction at the border desk.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: document mismatch, invasive review, denial of entry without custody. Higher risk here: the mismatch can also support lifetime inadmissibility, and one jurisdiction's facility rule is criminal with a documented arrest, which the anchor lacks.

Lower risk than this case: there, registry flags and an ineffective ombudsman produce delay without any criminal exposure. Here a mismatch can escalate to a fraud finding and detention, and facility exclusion is criminal in part of the territory, so this dossier sits below it.

Far above: that anchor has a directive that works on escalation and only rudeness as the residual harm. Here the operative document rule runs against the traveller, injunctions are partial, and custody harm is documented, so the gap is substantial.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system whose stages interlock. Documents are the entry point: a marker that does not match presentation is read as reasonable doubt, and a suspected wilful misrepresentation can convert an ordinary arrival into a permanent inadmissibility finding, or into detention. Once in custody, the documented treatment is severe, including forced labour and sexual abuse. On the ground, the operative rule varies by state: in most places there is no facility ban, but in a criminalising state an outed visitor can be arrested and held by birth sex, as happened in 2025. Offsetting this partially are a national hate-crime statute covering gender identity, working courts that have enjoined several measures, and police pursuit of the city's anti-trans violence. The state's own machinery, not street hostility, is the dominant exposure.
